Package neqsim.pvtsimulation.flowassurance

Class FloryHugginsAsphalteneModel

java.lang.Object
neqsim.pvtsimulation.flowassurance.FloryHugginsAsphalteneModel
public class FloryHugginsAsphalteneModel extends Object
Flory-Huggins regular solution model for asphaltene precipitation prediction.

This class implements the Flory-Huggins polymer solution theory applied to asphaltene precipitation, a widely-used approach in the petroleum industry. The model treats the oil as a solvent and asphaltenes as a dissolved polymer, using the mismatch in solubility parameters to predict precipitation.

Theoretical Background

The chemical potential of asphaltene in oil is expressed as: 

 ln(x_a * gamma_a) = ln(phi_a) + (1 - V_a / V_L) * (1 - phi_a) + (V_a / RT) * (delta_a - delta_L) ^ 2 * (1 - phi_a)
     ^ 2

Where:

  • x_a = mole fraction of asphaltene
  • phi_a = volume fraction of asphaltene
  • V_a, V_L = molar volumes of asphaltene and liquid (cm3/mol)
  • delta_a, delta_L = solubility parameters of asphaltene and liquid (MPa^0.5)
  • R = gas constant, T = temperature (K)

Onset occurs when delta_L drops below a critical value (typically when light ends evolve near bubble point).

Options

  • Oil solubility parameter: from the density correlation (default) or directly from the equation of state as delta_L = sqrt(-U_res / V) (FloryHugginsAsphalteneModel.SolubilityParameterMethod.EOS).
  • Calibration: calibrateToOnsetPressure(double, double) fits delta_a to a measured onset pressure. calibrateCorrelation(double) is a heuristic prior that uses no measured data.
  • Live-oil basis (default on): the asphaltene weight fraction is the fraction of the whole fluid; below the bubble point the concentration in the remaining oil rises as gas leaves.
  • Polydisperse asphaltene: setNumberOfAsphalteneFractions(int) splits the asphaltene into a gamma molecular-weight distribution; each fraction is compared with its own solubility limit.

Key Correlations

  • Oil solubility parameter from density: delta_L = A * rho + B (Lian et al., 1994)
  • Asphaltene solubility parameter: 19-24 MPa^0.5 (Barton, 1991)
  • Onset condition: delta_L = delta_onset (fitted parameter)

References:

  • Hirschberg, A. et al. (1984). SPE J., 24(3), 283-293.
  • Flory, P.J. (1953). Principles of Polymer Chemistry. Cornell Univ. Press.
  • Huggins, M.L. (1941). J. Chem. Phys., 9, 440.
  • Lian, H., Lin, J.R., Yen, T.F. (1994). Fuel, 73(3), 423-428.
  • Andersen, S.I., Speight, J.G. (1999). J. Petrol. Sci. Eng., 22, 53-66.

  • Method Details

    • configureFromAPIGravity

      public void configureFromAPIGravity(double apiGravity)
      Configures asphaltene properties based on API gravity.

      Uses correlations from Akbarzadeh et al. (2005) and Andersen and Speight (1999) to estimate asphaltene molecular weight, density, and solubility parameter from API gravity. Any earlier SARA adjustment is discarded.

      • Light oils (API > 35): Lower MW (500-700), higher delta (21-23 MPa^0.5)
      • Medium oils (25-35): Medium MW (700-1200), moderate delta (20-21 MPa^0.5)
      • Heavy oils (API < 25): Higher MW (1200-2500), lower delta (19-20 MPa^0.5)
      Parameters:
      apiGravity - API gravity of the crude oil

    • calibrateCorrelation

      public void calibrateCorrelation(double temperature)
      Heuristic prior for the delta_L correlation coefficient A. This uses no measured data.

      The method flashes the fluid at its own pressure and the given temperature, finds the solubility-parameter gap (delta_a - delta_L) at which the configured asphaltene content just reaches its solubility limit in that oil, and sets A so that the actual gap is 0.35 MPa^0.5 smaller. The fluid is then just stable at its own conditions and precipitates once depressurisation lowers delta_L by more than 0.35 MPa^0.5. The resulting onset follows from that choice of margin; when a measured onset pressure is available use calibrateToOnsetPressure(double, double) instead.

      Earlier versions used the liquid-liquid critical point chi_c = r (1 + 1/sqrt(r))^2 / 2 as the reference. That is not the onset condition of this model (solubility against a pure asphaltene phase), so the prior did not place the fluid near its onset.

      Parameters:
      temperature - reservoir temperature (K). Used for flash and chi calculation.

    • calibrateToOnsetPressure

      public double calibrateToOnsetPressure(double temperature, double measuredOnsetPressure)
      Calibrates the asphaltene solubility parameter so that precipitation starts exactly at a measured onset pressure.

      The liquid solubility parameter at the measured onset does not depend on delta_a, and the dissolved limit falls monotonically as delta_a moves away from delta_L, so delta_a is found by bisection on [delta_L, delta_L + 15]. Any earlier SARA adjustment is replaced by the calibrated value.

      Parameters:
      temperature - temperature of the measurement (K)
      measuredOnsetPressure - measured upper onset pressure (bara)
      Returns:
      the calibrated asphaltene solubility parameter (MPa^0.5)
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no system is set, the flash fails, or no delta_a in the range reproduces the onset

    • configureFromSARA

      public void configureFromSARA(double saturates, double aromatics, double resins, double asphaltenes)
      Configures asphaltene properties from SARA fractions.

      Sets the asphaltene weight fraction and scales the asphaltene solubility parameter for extreme resin/asphaltene ratios and very saturated oils. The scaling is applied to the value that was in place before the first SARA call, so calling this method more than once gives the same result as calling it once with the last arguments.

      Parameters:
      saturates - weight fraction of saturates
      aromatics - weight fraction of aromatics
      resins - weight fraction of resins
      asphaltenes - weight fraction of asphaltenes

    • calculateEosSolubilityParameter

      public static double calculateEosSolubilityParameter(PhaseInterface phase)
      Calculates the solubility parameter of an equation-of-state phase from its cohesive energy density.

      delta = sqrt(-U_res / V), with the residual internal energy U_res = H_res - (Z - 1) n R T at the phase temperature and volume. The phase must be initialised (init(2) or a flash followed by initProperties()).

      Parameters:
      phase - an initialised equation-of-state phase
      Returns:
      solubility parameter (MPa^0.5); NaN if the residual energy is not negative

    • calculateMaxDissolvedFraction

      public double calculateMaxDissolvedFraction(double deltaLiquid, double liquidMolarVolume, double temperature)
      Calculates the maximum dissolved asphaltene volume fraction (the solubility limit against a pure asphaltene phase).

      Solves ln(phi) + (1 - r)(1 - phi) + chi (1 - phi)^2 = 0 for the non-trivial root, with r = V_a / V_L. The equation is solved in u = ln(phi), which keeps very small solubilities accurate, and the trivial root phi = 1 is excluded explicitly. When the equation has no root below phi = 1 the asphaltene is fully miscible and 1 is returned.

      Parameters:
      deltaLiquid - liquid solubility parameter (MPa^0.5)
      liquidMolarVolume - liquid molar volume (cm3/mol)
      temperature - temperature (K)
      Returns:
      maximum dissolved asphaltene volume fraction (0 to 1)

      temperature - temperature (K)
      deltaAsphaltene - asphaltene solubility parameter (MPa^0.5)
      Returns:
      precipitated mass fraction

    • calculatePrecipitatedFraction

      public double calculatePrecipitatedFraction(double pressure, double temperature)
      Calculates the precipitated asphaltene mass fraction at given conditions.

      The asphaltene present in the oil is the configured weight fraction; with the live-oil basis (default) it is scaled by total mass / oil-phase mass, so below the bubble point it rises as gas leaves the oil. Each asphaltene fraction precipitates the amount above its own solubility limit.

      Parameters:
      pressure - pressure (bara)
      temperature - temperature (K)
      Returns:
      mass fraction of the oil that precipitates as asphaltene (0 = none); NaN if no system is set or the flash fails

    • calculateOnsetPressure

      public double calculateOnsetPressure(double temperature)
      Calculates the upper asphaltene onset pressure.

      Scans from the fluid's pressure down to 1 bara and bisects the first interval where the precipitated fraction exceeds the configured onset threshold.

      Parameters:
      temperature - temperature (K)
      Returns:
      onset pressure (bara), or NaN if no onset is found

    • setNumberOfAsphalteneFractions

      public void setNumberOfAsphalteneFractions(int numberOfFractions)
      Splits the asphaltene into a gamma molecular-weight distribution (mean = asphaltene MW, minimum = half of it, equal-mole slices). Each fraction has molar volume MW_i / rho_a and is compared with its own solubility limit; the fractions do not interact with each other (a simplification of the full multicomponent Flory-Huggins model).
      Parameters:
      numberOfFractions - number of fractions (1 restores the monodisperse model, maximum 20)
